content.page_title: Mechanical circulatory support and supportive therapies in advanced heart failure
content.summary: Discusses use of inotropes, management of diuretic resistance and kidney dysfunction, indications and types of mechanical circulatory support (MCS) including short-term and long-term use, and terminology for MCS strategies (see Table 15).

key_points: May improve hemodynamics, reduce congestion, augment cardiac output and peripheral perfusion.
Potentially prevent worsening end-organ function but not proven; may worsen myocardial ischemia or cause tachyarrhythmias.
Can be used palliatively when no other options exist.
Intermittent long-term outpatient inotrope use may be considered to improve functional class and quality of life.
Kidney dysfunction and loop diuretic resistance commonly characterize advanced heart failure.
Doubling loop diuretic dose is proposed initially, followed by concomitant administration of thiazides or metolazone.
Renal replacement therapies (e.g., ultrafiltration) should be considered for patients who fail diuretic strategies; effects on outcomes are unsettled.
MCS can improve survival and symptoms in patients with advanced heart failure.
Use of MCS should be considered based on specific clinical scenarios and INTERMACS profiles (see Table 14, Figure 4).
Indications for short- and long-term MCS depend on patient profile and goals (bridge to decision, bridge to recovery, bridge to transplantation, destination therapy, etc.).

indications: Reverse critical end-organ hypoperfusion and hypoxia in cardiogenic shock.
Used for a short, limited period (days to several weeks).
Support CNS and organ perfusion, reverse acidosis and multi-organ failure until recovery or decision on durable MCS/heart transplant.
uses: Bridge to decision (BTD), bridge to recovery (BTR), bridge to bridge (BTB) for long-term MCS or urgent transplant.
Considered for INTERMACS profiles 1 or 2 as bridge strategies.
considerations: Requires dedicated expertise and specific plans for stopping support.
May be used palliatively in some cases.
devices_examples: ECMO, Impella (device examples mentioned in table text)

indications: Selected patients when medical therapy is insufficient or short-term MCS did not lead to recovery.

To prolong life, improve quality of life, keep patient alive until transplantation (bridge to transplantation, BTT), reverse contraindications to transplant (bridge to candidacy, BTC), or as destination therapy (DT).

table_15_terms_descriptions.Bridge to decision (BTD) / Bridge to bri: Use of short-term MCS (ECMO or Impella) in cardiogenic shock until haemodynamics and end-organ perfusion are stabilized; evaluate contraindications for long-term MCS and other therapeutic options including long-term VAD or heart transplant.
table_15_terms_descriptions.Bridge to candidacy (BTC): Use of MCS (usually LVAD) to improve end-organ function and/or to make an ineligible patient eligible for heart transplantation.
